lesson_title: Write It So They Can Check It
hook_text: "Must be waterproof" means nothing to a factory. "No penetration in a five-minute drip test, hydrostatic head 1 500" means everything.
clip_script: This brief is not for you. It is for a supplier who never saw your tests and an inspector who has to check the roll. So every line has a number and a test. Water: nothing through in the drip test, dry under the thumb, hydrostatic head at least 1 500. Flame: three seconds in a candle, no flame, no drip, out in two seconds. Mass: under 350 grams a square metre so two people can carry the cover. Ripstop so a cut does not run. UV-stabilised so the sun does not make it brittle. Opaque at night, light on top. Welded seams. Eyelets every half metre, reinforced. Folds in frost, does not stick in heat. Then the limits: price, made in South Africa, two weeks, a thousand at a time. Run your samples through. Tarpaulin fails flame. Truck PVC is too heavy. Flame-retardant coated ripstop at 300 grams passes, at a price. Say which, say why, say what you could not test.
visual_style: Whiteboard page with ten numbered lines each gaining a number; a second column of constraints; sample squares crossed out one by one until one remains; a supplier and inspector icon reading the page.
mood: Precise and professional, writing for strangers.
pacing: Readers, ten lines, limits, elimination, verdict, each a beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write a specification a factory could quote against.
